title: Optimize small-n GEMM dispatch path (n≤128) to close per-call-overhead gap
description:
Reduce per-call constant overhead in `gf2-core`'s small-prime GEMM dispatch so n=64 cells clear the 1.5×-of-fflas `[hard]` bar that 662f7a15 had to amend to `[aspirational]`.

## Empirical motivation

662f7a15 closure (2026-05-06) amended GF(7)/GF(31) at n=64 from `[hard]` to `[aspirational]` because both cells miss the 1.5× target by 21–30%. The cause is per-call constant overhead, not algorithm. Verbatim from `662f7a15`'s description Amendment A:

> At n=64 the matrix is 64³ = 262k ops ≈ 14 µs of inner work; the per-call overhead (panel-pack allocation, OnceLock dispatch lookup, `try_simd_gemm_classical` dispatch tree, kernel prologue) is plausibly 5–8 µs (≥1/3 of wall time). The gap to fflas closes monotonically as n grows: 53% of fflas at n=64, 67% at n=256, 70% at n=1024, 80% at n=4096.

fflas-ffpack hits 36 Gop/s at GF(7)/n=64 vs our 19.36 — a 1.89× deficit. fflas has specialised small-matrix paths that pay much less per-call overhead.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] `cargo bench -p gf2-core --bench fieldmatrix_gemm -- "gemm/Fp_7/Fp_7/64"` and the GF(31)/n=64 sibling clear the 1.5×-of-fflas threshold (≥ 24.4 Gop/s and ≥ 24.1 Gop/s respectively) under 5-trial CCX1-pinned measurement (same methodology as `dev/bench_results/2026-05-06-662f7a15-prime-sweep-aggregate.csv`).
- [hard] No regression on n ∈ {256, 1024, 4096} cells (Candidate C bench output stays within 5% of pre-rework baseline measured at commit `687cff9`).
- [hard] Mersenne31 / Fp<65537> non-regression (delta ≤ 5%).
- [aspirational] GF(251) at n=64 clears the [aspirational] 3.2× soft threshold (≥ 20.1 Gop/s; currently 17.42).

## Implementation directions

Three structural levers identified during 662f7a15 closure:

1. **Per-thread arena allocation for panel-pack buffers**: `fp_small_try_gemm_classical` currently allocates `Vec<u8>` buffers per call (O(m·k + k·n) bytes). For n=64 that's ~8 KB allocations + memset. A thread-local arena (e.g. `thread_local! { static PACK_ARENA: RefCell<Vec<u8>> = RefCell::new(Vec::with_capacity(...)); }`) eliminates the per-call malloc/free.

2. **Inline dispatch tree**: `try_simd_gemm_classical` currently goes through `crate::simd::maybe_fp_small()` which is a `OnceLock::get_or_init` that incurs at least an atomic load per call. For small n where this overhead matters, the dispatch could be hoisted into the gemm caller (cache the function pointer in `FieldMatrix::gemm` per-call).

3. **Special-case n ≤ 128 path**: skip the panel-pack entirely for tiny matrices and call a register-blocked fixed-size kernel directly (e.g. 4×4×4, 8×8×8 micro-kernel). fflas's `MMHelper` has a similar branch for tiny dimensions.

The directions are not mutually exclusive; pick the highest-impact one(s) based on profiling.

## Out of scope

- Optimization for n ≥ 256 (already passes 1.5× target).
- Rewriting the inner kernel architecture (Candidate C / Candidate F selection is settled by 662f7a15 / b9aed0d8).
- Per-host tuning beyond the 5900X reference host.

## Authority and references

- 662f7a15 description (Amendment A) — empirical motivation, architectural-cause analysis.
- `dev/bench_results/2026-05-06-662f7a15-prime-sweep-aggregate.csv` — multi-trial bench evidence for n∈{256,1024} cells (confirming they PASS).
- `dev/bench_results/2026-05-06-662f7a15-rework2-perf-spiral-comparison.csv` — single-trial n=64 readings (the failing cells).
- `crates/gf2-core/src/gfp/simd_ops.rs::fp_small_try_gemm_classical` and `crates/gf2-core/src/lib.rs::simd::maybe_fp_small` — the dispatch hot path to optimize.
- `crates/gf2-kernels-simd/src/x86/fp_small.rs` — Candidate C kernel (entry points the small-n path would call directly without panel-pack).
